evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析：六; lines 114–125
evidence.text: The entry presents three competing explanations for 六: it may have once been graphically identical to 入 and later differentiated; it may depict a shelter and be an earlier graph for 廬; or it may be an early conventional counting mark. It considers the Shuowen 易-based explanation unlikely to preserve the graph’s original meaning. It cites oracle-bone examples for cardinal use (合集 32320, “燎六羊”) and ordinal use (合集 7775, “今六月王入于商”). These attest numeral use in the cited records but do not establish which origin theory is correct or the relative chronology of the senses.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：六

evidence.text: The file page identifies a digital vector depicting 六 in Shang oracle-script style and attributes its source to Sinica Database record 43.F555, noted as 合137 賓組. Commons describes the image as CC0 1.0/public domain. This is a modern digital reconstruction, not a photograph of an ancient artifact.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the official Xiaoxuetang landing page and attempted a character record and license notice. The queried character record did not load in an inspectable form; no Xiaoxuetang image is selected.

search_audit.outcome: Opened two candidate Commons file-description pages. Both identify modern vector reconstructions, Sinica Database sourcing, and CC0/public-domain licensing.
The official Unicode per-character endpoint returned an internal error. The Taiwan CNS11643 record opened and lists Mandarin liù, but is not a substitute for the prescribed Unihan click-through.

search_audit.outcome: Search found Western Zhou and Warring States bronze-style Commons candidates. Opened their description pages; selected only the Western Zhou bronze candidate for the proposed image set.

gaps: The graph’s origin remains unresolved among the 入-differentiation, shelter/廬, and counting-mark proposals. The consulted primary paleographic entry reports these as alternatives; the numeral-use examples do not decide among them.

The proposed shelter-name borrowing is not independently established: the depicted object’s name and pronunciation are unrecovered in the inspected evidence. The proposed loan from 廬 therefore remains unsupported as a sound-based explanation; no pronunciation match is inferred here.

CUHK cites oracle-bone cardinal and ordinal examples, but the original inscription images and exact dates of the individual records were not inspected. Their relative semantic chronology remains open.

The opened official Unihan endpoint for 六 was inaccessible, and the required current kMandarin reading was not verified from that record. The Taiwan CNS11643 record supports liù as modern Mandarin metadata only.
No exact character-specific Xiaoxuetang result or inspectable CC0 notice was retrieved in this run. Commons pages support the proposed image candidates and their stated licensing instead.

The proposed Commons images are modern digital drawings of ancient script forms, not photos of inscribed artifacts. Their labels indicate script traditions; the candidate files do not independently settle the graphic origin.

items.period: Shang oracle-script style; the file page points to Sinica record 43.F555, 合137 賓組
items.tradition: Oracle-bone script style; modern vector reconstruction
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction of 六 in Shang oracle-script style, associated by its source page with Sinica record 43.F555. The early graph is attested in numeral uses, while its original graphic explanation remains disputed.
items.alt: Black reconstructed oracle-script glyph for 六 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows an early script-style candidate relevant to the inscriptional numeral attestations while leaving the shelter and 入-related analyses unresolved.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page; attribution appreciated.

items.tradition: Bronze script style; modern vector reconstruction
items.caption: A modern vector reconstruction labelled Western Zhou bronze-script style, offering a later comparison with the Shang-style form. It illustrates a script tradition and does not resolve the competing origin proposals.
items.alt: Black reconstructed bronze-script glyph for 六 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Adds a later labelled script-style comparison without asserting a continuous, fully documented transformation.
items.rights: CC0 1.0 / public domain as stated on the Commons file page; attribution appreciated.

limitations.text: The image URLs use Wikimedia Commons’ Special:Redirect/file endpoint, which could not itself be opened by the web tool. The corresponding file-description pages were opened and provide the direct-file links, source descriptions, and reuse statements.

The selected glyphs are digital reconstructions, not artifact photographs. The oracle candidate’s source description cites a particular Sinica record, but the underlying record image was not independently inspected in this run.
